newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks languish on regional gloom.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks languish on regional gloom.

text.p: The Singapore stock market continued to languish at midday on Thursday, dampened by a regional gloom, dealers said.

"The big macro-picture doesn't look good for the whole region and Singapore is affected by this," said a dealer, who cited poor sentiment looming over Asian markets like Thailand, South Korea and Malaysia.
More exciting markets like the U.S. and Latin America are said luring foreign funds away from the region, dealers lamented.
"They are giving faster and better returns, which is why most people buy stocks, not for safe-haven," another dealer said.
He was referring to the safe-haven reputation Singapore market has given its stable government.
At midday, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 8.19 points at 1,985.30. Turnover was a moderate 47.96 million shares with 73 gainers to 158 losers.
